title: Keel's governance runs on forum posts and GitHub pull requests until the Powerhouse system supports Artifact edits
content:
Two clauses concede that the system the process depends on is not finished. A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.2 provides that "until the Powerhouse system supports submitting Artifact Edit Proposals, KEEL token holders may submit Artifact Edit Proposals by posting them to the Sky Forum" under the "Keel Prime" category, with a title containing "Keel Artifact Edit Proposal" and "cryptographic proof that the author controls an account holding the required percentage." A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.5.1 adds that until Powerhouse can update Artifacts, the Operational Facilitator "works with the Core Facilitator to update the Atlas GitHub repository" to reflect approved proposals.

The interesting part is which properties the fallback preserves and which it drops. Eligibility remains verifiable — the cryptographic proof replicates on-chain balance checking without the tooling — and discoverability is preserved by mandating an exact title string, effectively a hand-rolled index. What is lost is that the canonical Artifact temporarily lives in a git repository edited by two named facilitators, so the integrity of the record rests on repository access control rather than on the governance process itself.

Writing the fallback into the Artifact rather than treating it as informal practice is the notable governance move: the degraded mode is itself ratified, dated by its own "until" clause, and removable by the same Root Edit process it currently carries.
description: Transitionary measures substitute a titled Sky Forum post with cryptographic proof of holdings for proposal submission, and Core-Facilitator-assisted PRs to the next-gen-atlas repo for the edit
